method.title: Hear it. Understand it. Use it.
method.subtitle: Three steps, repeated until the words come out without you assembling them first.
method.s1Body: Every phrase starts as sound, not spelling. You listen first, replay as often as you like, and read it in Latin letters — no Arabic script required.
method.s2Body: Then the meaning: what it says literally, what it actually means, and when a Lebanese person would say it rather than the textbook version.
method.s3Title: Use it in a real conversation
method.s3Body: Finally you answer with it — choosing the natural reply, rebuilding the sentence, and repeating it across days until it's yours.
method.note: Situations, not word lists. You learn a phrase inside the conversation it belongs to, and meet it again a few days later when it's about to slip.

about.title: Born in Beirut. Teaching the Lebanon you won't find in a textbook.
about.p1: I grew up hearing five conversations at once around the same table — that's the Lebanese I teach. Whether you're calling your teta every Sunday, marrying into a Lebanese family, or finally booking that trip to Beirut, I'll get you talking, fast.
about.p2: Every lesson comes from real life: airport small talk, ordering man2ushe, arguing about who pays the bill.
about.note: Everything on this site is free — the lessons, the audio, all seven games. A class is the same thing, with someone listening and correcting you.
about.introBody: A few seconds of Lebanese, at the speed people actually speak it.
about.valueApproachBody: Situations first. You get the phrases a moment actually needs — a greeting, an order, a phone call — and use them out loud before you analyse them.
about.valueDialectBody: What you learn here is the dialect people speak day to day. Where the textbook version differs, I tell you which one to say and which one to only recognise.
about.valuePronunciationBody: Every phrase has audio and a Latin transliteration built for the sounds English doesn't have. In a class, you say it back and get corrected on the spot.
about.valueClassBody: You speak, I listen and correct, and we work through the situations you actually need. Bring what you didn't understand this week and we start there.
about.valueWhoBody: Complete beginners, heritage speakers who understand more than they say, and anyone who has done the free units and wants someone listening.
about.testimonialsPending: Real student quotes are on the way. Nothing invented goes here.

items.q: Do I need to read Arabic?
items.a: No. Every phrase on this site is written in Latin letters as well as Arabic script, and every phrase has audio. You can do the whole course without reading a word of Arabic.

No. Hkeeli teaches spoken Lebanese — the dialect people actually use with each other. Modern Standard Arabic is the written and broadcast language; it is not what you'll hear at a Lebanese dinner table.

items.q: Will I learn the Arabic alphabet?
items.a: Not as a goal here. The Arabic script sits next to every phrase, so you'll start recognising words if you want to — but the lessons, the games and the audio all work from transliteration.

items.q: Is this suitable for complete beginners?
items.a: Yes. Unit 1 starts at hello, and the Start Here questions will send you straight to it if you've never learned any Arabic.

items.q: What variety of Lebanese is taught?
items.a: Everyday spoken Lebanese, taught by a native speaker who grew up with it in Beirut. Where a phrase is casual, polite, affectionate or family-only, the lesson says so.

Classes are one-to-one, or a small group if you'd rather learn with someone you know. Send the booking form and you'll get a reply by email to agree a time; length, price and trial details are confirmed there.
Try the free mini-lesson on the home page. If you'd rather be pointed somewhere specific, answer the three questions on Start Here and you'll get one lesson or activity to begin with.
